threads.body: [Javaagent] Rejecting every bridge removes existing controller telemetry when the implementation is inherited from an uninstrumented superclass. For example, an annotated resource interface declares `Object get()`, an unannotated superclass supplies `public String get()`, and the resource subclass extends that superclass and implements the interface. javac declares only the forwarding `Object get()` bridge on the subclass. The superclass does not match the annotation instrumentation's type matcher, so excluding the bridge leaves interface dispatch without a controller span. The same problem affects accessibility bridges on public `@Path` resources inheriting an `@GET` method from a package-private superclass without `@Path`. Preserve bridges that are the only instrumentation point, while avoiding duplicate spans for same-class covariant implementations. Add installed-agent regression coverage for both inherited cases.

replies.body:
No code change.

The telemetry regression is not introduced by this PR. AgentInstaller.java:124 already uses Byte Buddy MethodGraph.Compiler.ForDeclaredMethods.INSTANCE before the PR (468480a3), and Byte Buddy 1.18.14 explicitly filters out isBridge() methods in that compiler. Installed-agent tests for both reported cases still emitted only the parent SERVER span with an experimental matcher that accepts inherited bridges. Replacing the matcher with its exact pre-PR implementation reproduced both missing-controller-span failures (2 tests, 2 failures). Changing this matcher alone cannot restore those spans; enabling bridge instrumentation would fix a separate pre-existing method-graph limitation. The original frozen-head matcher and installed-agent suites pass. No source change is warranted for the reported PR regression.
